mainEntity.name: What are the biggest risks that can derail a kitchen remodeling project, and how do I avoid them?

acceptedAnswer.text:
The biggest risks are unclear scope, under-budgeting, hidden structural or system issues, permit/inspection delays, and hiring the wrong contractor. Most major problems trace back to one of these. 
Context: Kitchens involve almost every trade—framing, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, cabinetry, and finishes—so mis-coordination or cutting corners can create safety issues, cost overruns, and long delays. 
Key factors:
- Starting without detailed plans, specs, and a written contract
- Choosing a low bid from an unlicensed or underinsured contractor
- Old wiring, plumbing, or water damage discovered during demo
- Changing the design mid-project without understanding cost/time impact
Practical guidance: Insist on a clear scope, itemized estimate, and signed change-order process before demo starts. Verify license, insurance, and references, and keep a 10–20% contingency fund for surprises. Soft positioning: An experienced contractor will help you spot common pitfalls early and build protections into the contract and schedule.
